recentItems.title: Can EVMs Be Hacked? : Suresh Kochattil EVM Vs Ballot Paper Controversy | Modi | Rahul Gandhi |iDream
recentItems.description:
#SureshKochattil, #EVMHacking, #ElectionCommission, #IndianElections, #VVPAT, #IndianDemocracy, #EVMTech, #IDreamInterviews,
Can EVMs Be Hacked? : Suresh Kochattil EVM Vs Ballot Paper Controversy | Modi | Rahul Gandhi |iDream

Evolution of Voting Systems: Traces the transition of Indian elections from traditional paper ballots and the dark days of rampant booth capturing (especially in the 1980s) to the introduction of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).

The Pilot Runs and Global Adoption: Highlights how EVMs were first introduced on a pilot basis in 1982 in Kerala, scaled up during Rajiv Gandhi's tenure in 1989 (Goa elections), and how countries worldwide—including Indonesia and Brazil—look up to India's robust electoral framework.

Standalone Technology & Security: Explains the engineering behind EVMs, emphasizing that they are standalone, chip-based devices (M1, M2, and M3 versions built by BEL and ECIL) with zero internet or external connectivity, making remote hacking physically impossible.

The Election Commission's Open Challenge: Recalls instances where the Election Commission challenged critics and tech experts to prove EVM tampering inside official controlled environments, noting that challenges failed to demonstrate any vulnerability.

Introduction of VVPAT: Details the integration of the Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT), allowing voters to physically verify their vote via a slip before it drops into the sealed box, ensuring 100% transparency.

Suresh Kochattil's Expert Insights: Guest expert Suresh Kochattil breaks down global comparisons (why countries like the USA use different systems), addresses common conspiracy theories, and details how technological modernization has streamlined counting and secured the democratic process.
